step2_renominate.invocation: scripts/discover_observables.py --rom 'roms/Journey to Silius (USA).nes' --state 'roms/Journey to Silius (USA)_start.state.bin' --profile configs/journey_to_silius.yaml --emit-solve --out runs/false_death_fanout/journey_to_silius/discover_journey_to_silius_fixed.json
step2_renominate.note: 0x00B9 no longer appears in the top-5 shown by find_hp_lives (top=6 truncation); a separate run with top=50 against the SAME probe sequence (identical evidence.nominated=70) confirms it is demoted, not removed: rank 10 of 24 groups, start=0, starts_nonzero=false -- exactly the sort-key behavior commit 158ec74 documents.

full_ranked_list_top9_with_starts_nonzer.note: the OLD nominee -- correctly demoted below every nonzero-start candidate

step3_verify_rank1.idle_200_steps: flat at 1, no free-run, no idle movement -- PASSES the idle check
step3_verify_rank1.right_hold_probe: FAILS: value drops 1 -> 0 within 4 steps (16 frames) of a bare RIGHT hold, with NO death, NO hazard contact, NO A/B press required. RIGHT+A and RIGHT+B reproduce the same 4-5 step drop. B-mash while stationary does NOT move it (rules out an ammo/shot counter). Conclusion: this byte transitions on the onset of rightward SCROLL/MOVEMENT itself (most likely a spawn-grace or intro-state flag), not on death.
step3_verify_rank1.verdict: DISQUALIFIED -- fires on ordinary forward movement, not death

step3_verify_other_ranked_candidates.0x000A: drops 2->0 at step 15 of plain RIGHT-hold; same movement-triggered pattern, just delayed (looks like a short invulnerability/spawn timer, not a life stock)
step3_verify_other_ranked_candidates.0x0001: cycles 0/1/3 with ~5-step period under RIGHT-hold -- an animation/frame counter, not a stock
step3_verify_other_ranked_candidates.0x012A: drops to 0 within 4 steps of RIGHT-hold, then free-runs UP to 34 later in the same 300-step hold -- fails 'does not free-run'
step3_verify_other_ranked_candidates.0x0502, 0x0012, 0x0053, 0x01A9, 0x027C: stable under a bare 300-step RIGHT-hold (good), but over a longer 2500-step randomized rollout (biased forward + occasional macros, matching the discovery tool's own death-drive recipe) none of them shows a clean single-drop-and-stay tied to an actual death: they wobble by small amounts (a few units) with no corroborating RAM-churn spike (max churn 244 across the whole 2500-step trace, no reload-sized event >300 ever observed) -- i.e. no verifiable death occurred in this rollout at all to correlate any byte against.
step3_verify_other_ranked_candidates.0x00B9_control: the OLD nominee also just flickers 0<->255 six times over the same 2500-step rollout with no correlated churn spike -- consistent with the bug report's own characterization: on this game domain, this signature is generically noisy and none of it should be trusted as 'death' without an independent event boundary.

step4_config_edit.reason: no verified better candidate. Rank-1 (0x0135) is empirically disqualified (fires on mere rightward movement); ranks 2-4 show the same or a related non-death signature; ranks 5-9 could not be corroborated against any observed death event in a 2500-step rollout. configs/journey_to_silius.yaml left untouched (lives: 0x00B9).

after_TRIAL_ONLY_not_kept.config_lives: 0x0135 (edited for this A/B measurement only, then reverted -- never committed)
after_TRIAL_ONLY_not_kept.interpretation: catastrophic collapse (774 -> 2 cells, 1269px -> 7px), NOT an improvement. Matches the direct-probe finding: 0x0135 reads start_lives=1 at root and drops to 0 on literally the first rightward-movement action any worker takes (this is a forced right-scroller, so 'the first action' is unavoidable), which GenericGame.is_dead's wrap-aware check (delta 1-8) reads as an instant death on essentially every rollout.

step5_measure_unblock.verdict: NULL / NEGATIVE RESULT, stated plainly. The fixed tool's #1 nomination for this profile is unusable -- worse than the original zero-start bug for this specific game, because it manufactures a false death on move #1 rather than after some exploration. The config was reverted and nothing from this trial is kept.

overall_verdict: Instrument gap, not a fix. Journey to Silius has no lives byte discoverable from this start state via the current death_drives probe methodology that survives direct behavioral verification. The zero-start defect (0x00B9) is real and confirmed, and the tool-level fix (commit 158ec74) correctly demoted it in the ranking -- but nothing else the probe surfaced behaves like a genuine death-triggered life stock; the probe's own 5 x 700-step death drives most likely never produced a real death for this ROM (no RAM-churn reload event was found in an independent 2500-step randomized rollout either), so every 'candidate' downstream of the demoted byte is coincidental small-amplitude RAM noise (spawn timers, animation counters, HUD digits), not lives. Config left unmodified. Nothing committed.
